job.title: Policy Officers, Capability Analysts, Strategic Communications Officers - EOI
job.description:
Chandler Macleod is seeking expressions of interest on behalf of our client for multiple opportunities supporting a nationally significant government program delivering complex policy, capability and strategic engagement outcomes.

These positions offer the chance to work on high-profile initiatives that influence Australia's strategic future, collaborating with government, industry and international stakeholders while contributing to major policy and capability objectives.

About the Role: Working within a fast-paced and collaborative environment, you will support the delivery of strategic outcomes across policy development, capability analysis and stakeholder engagement functions.

Key responsibilities may include:
  • Contributing to policy development, strategic analysis and capability initiatives.
  • Preparing high-quality briefs, submissions, reports and executive correspondence.
  • Supporting the delivery of advice to senior leaders and key decision-makers.
  • Assisting with policy implementation and program delivery activities.
  • Conducting research and analysis to support evidence-based decision making.
  • Building and maintaining effective relationships with internal and external stakeholders.
  • Supporting communications and engagement activities across a broad stakeholder network.
  • Coordinating meetings, events, consultations and engagement activities.
  • Working collaboratively across multidisciplinary teams to achieve shared outcomes.
About You To be successful, you will demonstrate:
  • Experience in policy, strategy, communications, research, analysis or program delivery.
  • Strong written communication skills with the ability to prepare clear and concise documentation.
  • Excellent stakeholder engagement and relationship management capabilities.
  • Sound analytical and problem-solving skills.
  • The ability to manage competing priorities and deliver quality outcomes within deadlines.
  • A proactive and adaptable approach to working in a dynamic environment.
  • Strong attention to detail and commitment to achieving results.
  • The ability to work both independently and collaboratively within a team environment.
What's on Offer
  • Opportunities across policy, capability analysis and strategic communications functions.
  • Exposure to complex and high-profile government initiatives.
  • Ongoing professional development and career growth opportunities.
  • Potential domestic and international travel opportunities.
  • Positions available in Canberra, Adelaide and Rockingham.
Essential Requirements
  • Australian Citizenship.
  • Ability to obtain and maintain a Negative Vetting Level 1 (NV1) Security Clearance.
If you are looking for an opportunity to contribute to nationally important work while developing your policy, analytical or communications career, we encourage you to apply.

job.title: Project Engineer- Marine
job.description:
Marine Project Engineer
  • Opportunity working at Rio Tinto
  • 12-month assignment via Chandler Macleod
  • Safety-first culture with supportive teams
About the Opportunity

Rio Tinto is a global mining and materials company operating in 35 countries, producing the materials essential to modern life. Their operations are built on safety, innovation, inclusion and creating value for communities, customers and shareholders.

Through Rio Tinto’s partnership with Chandler Macleod, we are seeking an experienced Project Engineer with Marine experience.

This is a newly created Project Engineer position supporting a major structural integrity program on the PPT Wharf in Dampier. Working on an 8:6 roster, you will oversee contractors, coordinate structural remediation works, manage quality and project documentation, and help deliver critical shutdown activities within a live operational marine environment. The role requires a self-motivated and adaptable professional who can navigate changing priorities, solve problems on the ground, and contribute to the successful delivery of this project.
 
Reporting to the Superintendent Delivery and working in a collaborative and exciting environment, you will:
  • Manage the day-to-day delivery of structural integrity works on a major wharf infrastructure project, ensuring scope, schedule and safety requirements are achieved.
  • Oversee contractor activities on site, providing direction, support and resolution of technical and operational issues as they arise.
  • Coordinate and monitor structural remediation works including blast and paint programs, structural steel repairs and replacement of beams and other infrastructure components.
  • Review, assess and respond to contractor technical queries, making practical engineering decisions in a fast-paced operational environment.
  • Conduct on-site verification of completed works, including quality inspections, quantity measurements and management of project documentation.
  • Support shutdown and outage execution activities, including schedule validation, stakeholder coordination and attendance at shutdown planning meetings.
  • Manage quality outcomes and defect close-out processes, ensuring compliance with project specifications and documentation requirements.
  • Adapt to changing project priorities, identifying alternative work scopes and maintaining project momentum when operational constraints or schedule changes impact planned activities.

About You
  • Proven structural integrity project experience in industrial or marine environments.
  • Proactive problem-solver with strong decision-making and adaptability.
  • Structural engineering qualification or relevant trade background with site delivery experience.
  • Resilient, hands-on professional who thrives in challenging operational environments.
  • Strong teamwork and communication skills
  • Dedication to everyone’s safety
  • Current C Class manual drivers’ license
  • Relevant trade qualifications and certificates
  • Ability to pass pre-employment medical and other testing
Why Join Chandler Macleod?
Chandler Macleod is one of Australia’s most experienced workforce partners. You’ll receive a competitive pay rate paid weekly, superannuation on all hours worked, access to our Employee Assistance Program, a dedicated Chandler-Rio Tinto support team, simple digital onboarding, and access to future Rio Tinto assignments.

Apply Now!
Ready to take the next step? Apply today to join Chandler Macleod for an exciting onsite assignment with Rio Tinto. Applications close 2 October 2026. Chandler Macleod reserves the right to close applications earlier if suitable candidates are identified.
 
At Chandler Macleod, we are committed to fostering a diverse workforce where everyone is welcome. We encourage applications from Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples, women, neurodiverse, people living with a disability and the LGBTIQA+ community. You can read more about our commitment to diversity and inclusion at https://www.chandlermacleod.com/diversity-and-incl

job.title: Operator (Wastewater)
job.description:
Opportunity for an experienced Civil Operator based in the Wastewater team in Canning vale. As part of the Perth Region Field Service team, you will be regularly outdoors, operating, inspecting and maintaining wastewater systems. 
 
About the role:
Operators are the frontline teams keeping essential water and wastewater services running across Western Australia. They respond to everything from routine maintenance and customer faults through to major incidents that make state-wide headlines.

 
What the role will involve:
  • Operate, maintain, monitor, and repair wastewater assets, operational sites and public facilities as required.
  • Carry out operation and maintenance tasks requiring use of specialist tools, plant, and equipment
  • Participate in safe job planning, team meetings and workplace inspections.
  • Demonstrate leadership by ensuring that all work is undertaken with safety as the priority in the provision of a work environment where no injury is considered acceptable, and all activities are undertaken without compromising health and safety.
  • Ability towork after hours and participate on a standby roster
 
Key skills and experience:
  • Able to work in a wastewater environment (sewage) – relevant vaccinations required
  • Western Australian “C” Class Drivers Licence, with a truck licence (MR or HR) being beneficial
  • Current Confined Space, Working at Heights, White Card and Gas Test Atmospheres tickets
  • Experience in water supply and wastewater systems
  • Required to be fully vaccinated with Hep A & B
  • Effective communication and interpersonal skills

job.title: Warehouse Associate
job.description:
Warehouse Worker with Amazon

  • Work at Amazon Australia’s Delivery Station located in Mayfield.
  • Training and ongoing support provided
  • Flexible work with variable shift length - most shifts are min 4-5 hours per shift however flex will be needed as per business requirements.
  • Shifts generally will start from 4AM-5AM and this site operates 7 days a week therefore minimum 5 days availability a week will be needed.

Your starting rate of pay is $35.14. You get paid penalties if you work afternoon, early morning or weekend shifts!

About the role
This is a casual role where you will be required to be available across 5 days per week (including 1 day on the weekend). We have day and night shifts available with each shift being 4-10 hours long and weekly hours averaging between 15 - 38hrs per week. Experience is not required for these positions and full training is provided, however, an ability to follow instructions and standard processes is a must.

Responsibilities
  • Sorting & labeling of parcels and boxes being sent to and from the warehouse
  • Storing/stowing received parcels and boxes throughout the facility
  • Picking parcels and boxes from shelves using an RF scanner (training provided)
  • Organising and dispatching parcels and boxes that will be sent to the customer
  • Cleaning and organisation of the site environment
  • Adhering to safety, quality and production standards
  • Standing and walking for extended periods
  • Lifting and moving products up to 23kg in weight

Successful applicants will be employed by Chandler Macleod to carry out a temporary work assignment to Amazon and will be required to complete background and police check and a drug and alcohol test. You must also have the right to work in Australia.

About Amazon
Amazon is a company with 20+ years of operational expertise and technology advancements, where the future of retail and logistics is becoming reality. Your role is key in enabling everyday deliveries for customers and being on the front line of fulfilling Amazon’s customer promise. In return Amazon offers a safe, inclusive and fun environment to set you up for success so you can work hard, have fun and make history.

job.title: Global Trade Compliance Specialist
job.description:
Join a leading Australian organisation operating in a highly regulated technology and defence-related environment.

We are seeking an experienced Trade Controls Specialist to lead trade compliance, export controls and regulatory assurance activities within a sophisticated and highly regulated operational environment. This position plays a key role in ensuring compliance with ITAR, EAR and Australian export control regulations while supporting business operations and risk management.


Responsibilities
  • Provide advice on trade compliance requirements for bids, projects, commercial activities and international transactions.
  • Manage export licences, approvals and regulatory submissions, including engagement with Australian and international stakeholders.
  • Oversee customs compliance, import/export activities and relationships with external customs and logistics providers.
  • Conduct compliance reviews, internal audits and trade control assurance activities, maintaining risk registers and reporting findings.
  • Maintain trade compliance records, licence documentation and reporting frameworks to support regulatory compliance and business operations.
  • Develop and deliver training, monitor regulatory changes and provide guidance to stakeholders across the business.

What We're Looking For
  • Demonstrated experience with ITAR, EAR and Australian export control or trade compliance regulations.
  • Experience supporting or managing export licences, regulatory approvals and engagement with relevant authorities.
  • Strong understanding of customs requirements, import/export processes and customs broker management.
  • Experience conducting compliance audits, assurance activities, risk assessments and legislative interpretation.
  • Ability to influence stakeholders, deliver training and communicate complex regulatory requirements effectively.
  • Australian citizenship and ability to obtain or hold an Australian Defence security clearance. Experience with Technical Assistance Agreements, US export licensing systems, or qualifications in Business, Commerce or Law will be highly regarded.

The Opportunity
  • Part-time position (24 hours per week)
  • Based in Inner North Brisbane
  • Flexible working arrangements and genuine work-life balance
  • Standalone specialist role with broad business exposure and influence
  • Opportunity to influence compliance outcomes on complex projects within a technically advanced and highly regulated industry
  • Open to experienced professionals seeking either part-time flexibility or a return to a dedicated trade compliance career path

For a confidential discussion or to express your interest, please apply now.

job.title: EOI - Procurement & Contracting Manager
job.description:
Chandler Macleod is seeking expressions of interest from experienced procurement and contracting professionals to join a Federal Government agency.

Location: Australia-wide, with flexible and on-site arrangements

About the opportunity
Our client is a large, high-profile Federal Government agency delivering a long-term program of national significance. It is building its commercial capability and wants talented procurement and contracting leaders to join as ongoing APS employees.
The agency's Commercial Branch runs the procurement and contracting function end to end. Its services include:
  • Supporting procurements from the moment a business area identifies a need through to contract execution and ongoing contract management
  • Providing guidance, assurance and advice on procurement policy and methods
  • Advising on probity matters, requirements and activities
  • Liaising with specialist services such as legal, where required
The role
As a Procurement & Contracting Manager, you will lead a team delivering complex procurement and contract management activities. You will work with considerable independence and be the go-to adviser for business areas on commercial matters.

Key duties may include:
  • Providing guidance and support across procurement planning, tendering, contract formation and contract management, ensuring compliance with legislation, the Commonwealth Procurement Rules and internal policies
  • Reviewing complex to very complex contracting documents, including commercially sensitive reports, submissions and contract change proposals
  • Leading and managing a team: setting clear performance and behavioural standards, delegating work, managing performance and developing people
  • Advising stakeholders across procurement, commercial, legal and financial matters to achieve sound contract outcomes
  • Identifying and managing commercial risks, including supplier performance and compliance with mandatory requirements
  • Building strong working relationships with internal stakeholders, suppliers and specialist advisers
Ideal candidate
The agency is looking for people who are agile, innovative and energised by fast-paced work. You will be able to demonstrate:
  • Strong skills and hands-on experience in procurement and contracting
  • The ability to work in an integrated environment and build collaborative relationships
  • High-level organisational skills, with the drive to set clear procurement and contract management plans and timeframes
  • A positive response to change and uncertainty
  • A track record of working effectively in teams and/or leading a team
  • The ability to turn strategic objectives into practical initiatives
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills
Desirable qualifications and experience
  • Experience applying Commonwealth commercial frameworks, including the Commonwealth Procurement Rules, to complex procurement requirements (highly desirable)
  • A relevant qualification in procurement, contract management or a related discipline, or equivalent significant experience
  • Experience in a large Federal Government agency or a complex, high-value commercial environment

Eligibility and how to express interest
To be eligible, you must be an Australian citizen and be able to obtain and maintain a Negative Vetting Level 1 (NV1) security clearance. Holding a current clearance is highly regarded.
To express interest, please submit:
  1. Your current resume
  2. A short statement (no more than one page) outlining your procurement and contracting experience and why you are suited to this role
  3. Details of any current security clearance

Key Criteria To be successful in this role, you will demonstrate:

  • Strong capability applying human-centred design, service design and business design methodologies
  • Experience analysing current-state operations and designing future-state business processes, services and operating models
  • Proven workshop facilitation and stakeholder engagement skills across business and technical teams
  • Strong analytical and systems-thinking capability
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to present complex information clearly
  • Experience developing operating models, capability maps, service blueprints and process models

Details:

job.title: Project Manager
job.description:

6-month contract | Brisbane CBD | $96-$106/hr + Super | Possible Hybrid working available

job.title: Steel Fixers
job.description:
About the role
Great opportunity for experienced Steel Fixers to join a busy precast yard in Woolgoolga, NSW. You’ll be working hands-on with reinforcement steel for precast moulds—reading drawings, preparing and tying rebar, and ensuring reinforcement is set correctly prior to concrete pours.

 
Duties
  • Read reinforcing steel drawings and specifications
  • Measure, cut and bend reinforcing bar (rebar) to required sizes
  • Assemble and fix reinforcement cages and steel frames
  • Tie reinforcement using tie wire and hand tools
  • Position reinforcement, mesh, starter bars, ligatures and components inside precast moulds
  • Install spacers and maintain required concrete cover
  • Check dimensions, spacing and positioning against drawings
  • Operate tools/equipment (rebar cutters, benders, grinders, tying tools)
  • Assist with setting up and stripping precast moulds as required
  • Move/position reinforcing steel and materials around the yard
  • Maintain a clean, safe work area and follow WHS procedures/PPE requirements
  • Work closely with concrete crews, formworkers, and crane/production teams to prepare moulds for pouring
 
Skills and Experience
  • Proven steel fixing experience (ideally within precast or similar production environments)
  • Ability to read and work from reo/reinforcement drawings and specs
  • Confident cutting, bending, tying, and placing reo to measurement/tolerance requirements
  • Strong safety mindset and ability to work efficiently in a team environment
 
Desirable:
  • Experience working in precast yards / mould preparation environments
  • Ability to operate common yard tools and equipment safely (cutters/benders/grinders)
 
Benefits
  • Competitive hourly rate ($45–$50/hr + super, depending on skills & experience)
  • Full-time hours (40 hours/week)
  • Local Woolgoolga role with an established precast operation
 
How to apply
Sound interesting? We would love to hear from you! Click APPLY NOW to upload a copy of your current resume & cover letter, or call Neva on 02 6691 9101 for a confidential discussion.

Chandler Macleod is recruiting on behalf of our client for an experienced Program Management Office (PMO) Assurance Officer to support the delivery of critical capability programs within a highly secure Federal Government environment.


This is an exciting opportunity to join a dynamic PMO team responsible for providing assurance, governance, reporting, risk oversight, test and evaluation support, and performance monitoring across a complex project and program portfolio. You will work closely with project teams, technical specialists and senior stakeholders to ensure capability outcomes are delivered effectively, risks are managed, and governance obligations are met.

  • Support assurance activities across projects, programs and portfolios to provide confidence in capability delivery outcomes.

  • Undertake testing, assessments and analysis activities to evaluate project performance and delivery confidence.
  • Support capability test, evaluation and readiness activities.

  • Assist with identifying delivery risks, issues, opportunities and improvement initiatives.
  • Support the continuous improvement of assurance, governance and portfolio management practices.

Key Responsibilities Risk Assurance
  • Maintain portfolio risk registers and reporting products.
  • Monitor risk treatments, mitigation activities and reporting obligations.
  • Analyse project and program risks, identifying trends, emerging issues and escalation requirements.
  • Support effective risk management and assurance practices across the portfolio.

Financial Assurance
  • Assist with assessments of project financial performance, affordability and funding utilisation.
  • Analyse project financial information and contribute to portfolio-level reporting and insights.
  • Support assurance reviews of business cases, investment proposals and financial governance activities.

Test and Evaluation Assurance
  • Coordinate and support test and evaluation assurance activities.
  • Assist with readiness assessments and evidence collection activities.
  • Monitor assurance actions and maintain assurance records and documentation.
  • Contribute to reporting that supports capability readiness and deployment confidence.

Delivery Health and Benefits Assurance
  • Support project and program health assessments through analysis of delivery performance information.
  • Monitor benefits realisation activities and improvement initiatives.
  • Contribute to portfolio performance reporting and trend analysis.
  • Support assurance reviews that improve program delivery outcomes and governance effectiveness.

Key Criteria to be Successful To be successful in this role, you will demonstrate:
  • Experience supporting PMO, portfolio, program or project assurance functions within complex delivery environments.
  • Strong understanding of governance, assurance, risk management and portfolio reporting practices.
  • Experience conducting assessments, reviews and analysis to support project and program oversight.
  • Ability to evaluate project performance and provide recommendations for improvement.
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with the ability to synthesise complex information from multiple sources.
  • Experience preparing executive reports, governance documentation and assurance findings.
  • Ability to apply frameworks, methodologies, policies and standards consistently across delivery activities.
  • Strong stakeholder engagement skills, with the ability to work collaboratively across technical and business teams.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
  • Strong organisational skills with the ability to manage multiple priorities and competing deadlines.

Desirable Experience
  • Experience within Defence, National Security or Federal Government environments.
  • Knowledge of project assurance, quality assurance, test and evaluation frameworks.
  • Exposure to portfolio management, program delivery and enterprise governance practices.
  • Experience supporting benefits realisation, delivery health assessments and performance reporting.
  • Understanding of risk management and project financial assurance processes.
  • Experience working within complex ICT or capability delivery programs.

Security Requirements
  • Current TSPV Security Clearance is mandatory.

Role Details
  • Position: Program Management Office (PMO) Assurance Officer
  • Locations: Canberra ACT, Melbourne VIC, Brisbane QLD
  • Working Arrangement: Onsite
  • Hours: Up to 40 hours per week
  • Contract: 12-Month Initial Contract + 12-Month Extension Option

job.description:

This is an exciting 12-month assignment supporting people with disability, their families, carers, and communities to access information, services, and supports.

Working within a community-focused environment, you will play a key role in building relationships, promoting inclusion, and supporting individuals to connect with the National Disability Insurance Scheme (NDIS) and broader community services.

  • Albany, WA

About the Role As a Local Community Connector, you will provide a visible, local presence within the community and support people to navigate available services and pathways. job.title: Program Management Office (PMO) Assurance Officer
job.description:
Chandler Macleod is recruiting on behalf of our client for an experienced Program Management Office (PMO) Assurance Officer to support the delivery of critical capability programs within a highly secure Federal Government environment.


This is an exciting opportunity to join a dynamic PMO team responsible for providing assurance, governance, reporting, risk oversight, test and evaluation support, and performance monitoring across a complex project and program portfolio. You will work closely with project teams, technical specialists and senior stakeholders to ensure capability outcomes are delivered effectively, risks are managed, and governance obligations are met.


This role is ideally suited to a PMO, Assurance, Governance, Risk, Portfolio Management or Program Management professional who enjoys working in complex delivery environments and driving continuous improvement across project and portfolio performance.

About the Role In this position, you will:
  • Support assurance activities across projects, programs and portfolios to provide confidence in capability delivery outcomes.
  • Coordinate assurance reviews, governance activities and reporting requirements across multiple workstreams.
  • Undertake testing, assessments and analysis activities to evaluate project performance and delivery confidence.
  • Support capability test, evaluation and readiness activities.
  • Engage with project, program and technical stakeholders to gather, analyse and evaluate complex information.
  • Contribute to executive reporting, portfolio insights and governance documentation.
  • Apply established assurance frameworks, methodologies, processes and controls.
  • Support portfolio reporting and decision-making through research, analysis and performance monitoring.
  • Assist with identifying delivery risks, issues, opportunities and improvement initiatives.
  • Support the continuous improvement of assurance, governance and portfolio management practices.

Key Responsibilities Risk Assurance
  • Maintain portfolio risk registers and reporting products.
  • Monitor risk treatments, mitigation activities and reporting obligations.
  • Analyse project and program risks, identifying trends, emerging issues and escalation requirements.
  • Support effective risk management and assurance practices across the portfolio.

Financial Assurance
  • Assist with assessments of project financial performance, affordability and funding utilisation.
  • Analyse project financial information and contribute to portfolio-level reporting and insights.
  • Support assurance reviews of business cases, investment proposals and financial governance activities.

Test and Evaluation Assurance
  • Coordinate and support test and evaluation assurance activities.
  • Assist with readiness assessments and evidence collection activities.
  • Monitor assurance actions and maintain assurance records and documentation.
  • Contribute to reporting that supports capability readiness and deployment confidence.

Delivery Health and Benefits Assurance
  • Support project and program health assessments through analysis of delivery performance information.
  • Monitor benefits realisation activities and improvement initiatives.
  • Contribute to portfolio performance reporting and trend analysis.
  • Support assurance reviews that improve program delivery outcomes and governance effectiveness.

Key Criteria to be Successful To be successful in this role, you will demonstrate:
  • Experience supporting PMO, portfolio, program or project assurance functions within complex delivery environments.
  • Strong understanding of governance, assurance, risk management and portfolio reporting practices.
  • Experience conducting assessments, reviews and analysis to support project and program oversight.
  • Ability to evaluate project performance and provide recommendations for improvement.
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with the ability to synthesise complex information from multiple sources.
  • Experience preparing executive reports, governance documentation and assurance findings.
  • Ability to apply frameworks, methodologies, policies and standards consistently across delivery activities.
  • Strong stakeholder engagement skills, with the ability to work collaboratively across technical and business teams.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
  • Strong organisational skills with the ability to manage multiple priorities and competing deadlines.

Desirable Experience
  • Experience within Defence, National Security or Federal Government environments.
  • Knowledge of project assurance, quality assurance, test and evaluation frameworks.
  • Exposure to portfolio management, program delivery and enterprise governance practices.
  • Experience supporting benefits realisation, delivery health assessments and performance reporting.
  • Understanding of risk management and project financial assurance processes.
  • Experience working within complex ICT or capability delivery programs.

Security Requirements
  • Current TSPV Security Clearance is mandatory.

Role Details
  • Position: Program Management Office (PMO) Assurance Officer
  • Locations: Canberra ACT, Melbourne VIC, Brisbane QLD
  • Working Arrangement: Onsite
  • Hours: Up to 40 hours per week
  • Contract: 12-Month Initial Contract + 12-Month Extension Option
  • Start Date: January 2027

Why Apply? This is a unique opportunity to contribute to nationally significant capability programs while working alongside experienced project, portfolio and assurance professionals in a highly secure environment. You will play a critical role in strengthening governance, assurance and delivery confidence across complex strategic initiatives.

If you have a strong background in PMO, governance, assurance, risk or portfolio management and are looking for your next challenge, we encourage you to apply.


At Chandler Macleod, we are committed to fostering a diverse workforce where everyone is welcome. We encourage applications from Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples, women, neurodiverse, people living with a disability and the LGBTIQA+ community.

You can read more about our commitment to diversity and inclusion at https://www.chandlermacleod.com/diversity-and-inclusion.

job.title: Instructional Designer
job.description:
Government Instructional Designer (6-Month Contract with Possible Extension)
Location: Fortitude Valley
Start Date: November 2, 2026
End Date: May 31, 2027 (with potential extension)

Are you an experienced Instructional Designer passionate about creating impactful learning experiences? We are seeking a dedicated professional to join a government team on a temporary basis, working to develop engaging and effective learning resources that support organizational objectives and enhance learner outcomes.

About the Role:
The primary purpose of this role is to facilitate learning by designing and developing a wide range of digital and face-to-face learning resources grounded in adult learning principles. Working closely with subject matter experts and key stakeholders, you will create tailored, fit-for-purpose e-learning programs and other instructional materials that meet performance needs and learner requirements.

Key Responsibilities:
  • Design, develop, maintain, and update eLearning programs and digital learning resources using Articulate 360 and associated technologies.
  • Partner with subject matter experts (SMEs) and stakeholders to analyze content, extract critical information, and translate complex concepts into engaging, learner-centered solutions.
  • Conduct consultation, discovery, and sense-making activities to identify learning requirements, performance gaps, and target audiences.
  • Develop comprehensive learning strategies, recommending suitable delivery methods including eLearning, blended learning, virtual sessions, face-to-face workshops, videos, job aids, and performance support resources.
  • Produce multimedia learning assets such as instructional videos, screen recordings, simulations, and demonstrations using tools like Camtasia.
  • Analyze audience and business needs to determine the most appropriate content structure, learning approach, and assessment methodologies.
  • Create learning objectives, storyboards, scripts, assessments, and evaluation tools to measure learning effectiveness.
  • Collaborate with facilitators and operational teams to develop facilitator guides, participant workbooks, presentation materials, and supporting resources for classroom and blended programs.
About You:
  • Proven experience in instructional design and e-learning development.
  • Expertise with Articulate 360, Camtasia, and other digital media tools.
  • Strong understanding of adult learning principles and instructional design models.
  • Ability to analyze content, performance gaps, and audience needs to produce targeted learning solutions.
  • Skilled in developing multimedia assets and engaging instructional content.
  • Excellent collaboration and communication skills.
Nice to Have:
  • Experience working within government or similar organizational environments.
  • Knowledge of various delivery methods including virtual and face-to-face training.
  • Familiarity with multimedia production and assessment development.
 
Apply now to be considered for this exciting opportunity.

job.title: Senior Technical Lead
job.description:
About the company:

This Federal Government agency works to deliver programs and services that support people with disability and their families, aiming to improve access, engagement, and outcomes across Australia. The agency collaborates closely with communities, service providers, and government stakeholders to implement initiatives that enhance social inclusion, wellbeing, and equity.

About the Team

The Future State Modelling team supports the agency with major workforce changes and future planning. The team uses data, modelling and analysis to understand future workforce needs and help the agency plan how to get there.
The team provides workforce forecasts, different scenarios and analysis to support important business decisions. It brings together technical, analytical and strategic skills to solve complex workforce challenges and develop better ways of working.

About the Role
The Senior Data Technician provides technical leadership across workforce modelling, forecasting and analytics.
The role involves designing, developing and improving modelling and analytical solutions that support workforce planning and reform. The successful candidate will work with complex workforce, policy and operational information and turn it into practical, reliable tools and insights to support decision-making.
The role also focuses on building the capability of the wider team through mentoring, knowledge sharing and developing consistent technical standards and processes.


Key Responsibilities
 
  • Design, develop and maintain workforce modelling, forecasting and analytical solutions.
  • Turn complex workforce, policy and operational issues into practical and reliable technical solutions.
  • Use Microsoft and other approved technology to develop modelling and analytical tools.
  • Apply strong technical, development and problem-solving skills to complex projects.
  • Develop and maintain technical standards, documentation, testing and quality assurance processes.
  • Ensure modelling and analytical products are accurate, reliable, transparent and easy to maintain.
  • Provide technical leadership, mentoring and guidance to team members.
  • Share knowledge and help build the technical and analytical skills of the team.
  • Develop reusable solutions and consistent modelling practices.
  • Work with stakeholders to understand their needs and deliver practical outcomes.
  • Identify and manage risks within their area of responsibility.

You Must Have
 
  • Strong experience in data, analytics, workforce modelling, forecasting or a similar technical field.
  • Advanced technical and problem-solving skills.
  • Experience designing, developing and maintaining analytical or modelling solutions.
  • Strong systems thinking and the ability to turn complex problems into practical solutions.
  • Experience working with Microsoft tools and enterprise technology.
  • Experience with technical documentation, testing, quality assurance and governance.
  • The ability to work independently and make sound technical decisions.
  • Strong communication and stakeholder management skills.
  • Experience mentoring, coaching or supporting other team members.
  • The ability to work effectively in a changing environment and develop creative solutions to technical challenges.

Benefits:
  • ASAP start (pending Federal Police Clearance)
  • Assignment end date: 31st December 2027 
  • Location:  Geelong VIC, Melbourne VIC, Newcastle NSW, Surry Hills NSW, and Brisbane QLD
  • $602.55/Daily (excluding super)

How to apply:

Chandler Macleod is an equal opportunity employer as part of our commitment to creating a diverse and inclusive workplace, Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people, disability and culturally and linguistics candidates are also encouraged to apply.

Please note the successful candidate for the role must hold Australian Citizenship.

Application closes on the 29th September 2026

job.title: Coordinator PMO
job.description:
Coordinator - Project Management Office (MPO)
Blackburn | Hybrid Working (2 Days Office)
$65 per hour + Super
Full-Time | 38 Hours Per Week
3-Month Contract (Until 18 December 2026)

An exciting opportunity is available for an experienced Coordinator - MPO to join a major transformation project focused on the implementation of a new Project Management Tool.
This role will play a key part in supporting project governance, stakeholder engagement, reporting, training, financial administration, and project coordination activities to help deliver successful business outcomes.

About the Role
Working closely with Project Managers, business stakeholders, and vendors, you will provide end-to-end project coordination support across transformation and strategic initiatives. You will assist in driving project delivery by ensuring effective governance processes, project documentation, reporting, risk management, stakeholder communication, and operational support.

Key Responsibilities
  • Coordinate project activities to ensure delivery against agreed timelines, budgets, quality standards, and project objectives.
  • Develop and maintain key project documentation, including risk and issue registers, stakeholder management plans, communication plans, and project schedules.
  • Prepare steering committee papers, meeting agendas, minutes, and project status reports.
  • Coordinate meetings and provide administrative support across project teams, vendors, and internal stakeholders.
  • Assist with budgeting, forecasting, invoicing, and financial reporting activities.
  • Monitor project risks and issues and provide recommendations to support project success.
  • Support the development of training materials and change management activities to enable smooth adoption of new tools and processes.
  • Undertake research, data analysis, and reporting to support informed decision-making.
  • Maintain strong stakeholder relationships and ensure clear communication throughout project lifecycles.
  • Assist with the development and review of project-related policies, procedures, and processes.
About You
To be successful in this role, you will demonstrate:
  • Experience in project coordination or project management environments.
  • Strong project reporting and administration skills.
  • Advanced proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite.
  • Strong Power BI skills, including reporting and data visualisation.
  • Excellent stakeholder engagement and communication abilities.
  • Experience supporting governance forums, steering committees, and project documentation.

job.description:
Dispatch Worker
 
Join Our Dynamic Dispatch Team in the Poultry Industry!
We are currently seeking reliable and hardworking Dispatch Workers, with a forklift licence desirable, to join our client's dispatch team working in the poultry industry. This role offers an exciting opportunity to contribute to a leading industry operation, ensuring the smooth flow of stock through unpacking, packing, transporting stock, and some forklift operation.
You will be working in a fast-paced production environment, which requires a high level of attention to detail, the ability to meet strict deadlines, and a strong commitment to safety and efficiency. If you thrive in energetic settings and take pride in your work, this position is perfect for you.
We offer full training and PPE to all of our employees, as well as free parking and award rates. Our facility operates in a refrigerated environment, ensuring that all products meet the highest possible standards.
 
What You Will Need

  • Current LF forklift licence (desirable)

job.title: Technical Estimator
job.description:
Employment Type: Full-Time, Casual 
Length of Assignment: Two weeks with potential extension
Working Arrangement: 100% on-site, Bayswater
Hourly Rate: $58.75-$67.5 per hour + Super

About the Role
Our client is seeking an experienced Technical Estimator professional to join the team on an initial two-week contract, with the possibility of extension.

This role will suit someone with a strong background in timber, steel or manufacturing environments, combined with proven experience in estimating and quotations within the timber, steel or related building products sectors.

The successful candidate will be confident interpreting architectural plans, taking measurements, preparing quotations and communicating professionally with builders, joinery companies and other industry stakeholders.

You will play an important role in understanding project requirements, interpreting floor plans and determining the appropriate door and joinery requirements before preparing accurate quotations.
 
Key Responsibilities
  • Review and interpret architectural drawings and floor plans to identify door and joinery requirements.
  • Take and interpret measurements to determine appropriate door sizes, specifications and quantities.
  • Assess architectural drawings and specifications to determine appropriate door systems, mouldings, architraves and joinery-related solutions.
  • Prepare accurate and competitive quotes for builders and other customers.
  • Liaise with builders, contractors, suppliers and customers to project requirements.
  • Provide professional and confident communication over the phone and via email.
  • Use CAD and related design/technical software to interpret and support project requirements.
  • Work with 3CX phone systems and associated communication platforms.
  • Understand manufacturing processes and how design and specifications translate into production.
  • Work with and understand CNC manufacturing processes, including 5-axis CNC machinery.
  • Assist with general technical and estimating requirements across timber, steel and door manufacturing.
  • Ensure quotations and measurements are accurate and aligned with project specifications.
 
 
Skills and Experience
  • Previous experience within timber manufacturing, joinery, doors or a related manufacturing environment.
  • Previous experience in estimating and quoting
  • Strong ability to read and interpret architectural drawings and floor plans.
  • Confidence taking measurements and determining appropriate product requirements.
  • Experience working with CAD or CAD-related software.
  • Knowledge and experience with CNC machinery, particularly 5-axis machines.
  • Strong computer literacy.
  • Excellent phone manner and confident verbal communication skills.
  • Strong attention to detail and accuracy when preparing quotes.
  • The ability to make practical decisions based on drawings, measurements and project requirements.
  • A proactive approach and the ability to work independently

  • Identify process improvements, system dependencies, risks and opportunities.
  • Support system design, testing, implementation and defect resolution activities.
  • Collaborate with business and technical teams to define requirements and solutions.
  • Develop user guides, training materials and operational procedures.
  • Contribute to implementation planning, change activities and continuous improvement initiatives.
Key Criteria to be successful in this role, you will demonstrate:
  • Proven experience as a Business Analyst delivering process improvement and systems transformation initiatives.
  • Strong capability in business process mapping, workflow design and requirements gathering.
  • Experience supporting system implementation, testing and change activities.
  • Highly developed analytical and problem-solving skills with the ability to identify risks, dependencies and practical solutions.
  • Strong stakeholder engagement skills with the ability to work effectively across business and technical teams.
  • Excellent written communication skills, including the development of process documentation, procedures and user guides.
  • Advanced skills across Microsoft 365 and business systems environments.
  • Ability to manage competing priorities and deliver quality outcomes within agreed timeframes.
Desirable Experience
  • Experience in finance, procurement, contract management, CRM, event management or project management systems.
  • Qualifications in Business Analysis, Information Systems, Project Management or a related discipline.
  • Exposure to platforms such as Salesforce, TechnologyOne, SharePoint or similar enterprise systems.

If you are a proactive Business Analyst with a passion for process improvement, stakeholder engagement and delivering meaningful business change, we encourage you to apply.

job.title: Senior Health & Safety Advisor
job.description:
Our client is seeking an experienced Senior Health & Safety Advisor (HSE Advisor / WHS Advisor) to join their team on an initial 3-month contract, with the possibility of extension based on business requirements.
This is a site-based role working primarily  in Cockburn. Reporting to the Head of Safety, you will work alongside two experienced team members to provide expert Health, Safety and Risk Management support across operations.

Key Responsibilities
  • Provide expert Health & Safety, WHS and HSE advice to site teams and leaders.
  • Support hazard identification, risk assessments and risk management activities.
  • Coach and influence stakeholders to promote positive safety behaviours and outcomes.
  • Conduct incident investigations, analyse findings and identify corrective actions.
  • Assist with management of hazards, corrective actions and safety reporting systems.
  • Build strong relationships with operational teams and contractors.
  • Promote continuous improvement initiatives and best-practice safety outcomes.
  • Support compliance with WHS legislation, company policies and safety procedures.
  • Contribute to the ongoing development of a strong safety culture across site operations.
About You
To be successful in this Health & Safety Advisor role, you will have:
  • Previous experience as a Health & Safety Advisor, HSE Advisor, WHS Advisor or Safety Advisor.
  • Tertiary qualification in Health and Safety or related studies (Bachelor, Masters, Grad Dip., Grad Cert.) or Diploma or Cert IV in Health and Safety.
  • Minimum 2 years industry experience in the power generation or resourcing sectors.
  • Incident Cause Analysis Method (ICAM) Lead Facilitator trained (or competence supporting investigations if non-ICAM methodology - Highly preferred
  • A coaching mindset with the ability to influence and guide others without relying on authority.
  • Confidence engaging with personnel at all levels of the business.
  • Strong understanding of risk management principles, including consequence and likelihood assessments.
  • Experience using Health & Safety Management Systems and digital reporting tools.
What's on Offer
  • Initial 3-month contract with potential for extension.
  • Opportunity to work within a critical power generation environment.
  • Collaborative and supportive safety team.
  • Diverse stakeholder engagement across multiple operational sites.
  • Competitive hourly rate.
  • Fully onsite role with direct engagement across site operations.
If you're a proactive Health & Safety professional who enjoys coaching, influencing and driving positive safety outcomes, we'd love to hear from you. Apply today.

job.title: Fabricator/Boiler Maker
job.description:
Heavy Fabrication & Welding TradespeopleAPS Welding | Inverell, NSW
$35–$50 per hour  (open to negotiation - tell us what you're worth!) + overtime | 38-hour standard week | Immediate start
APS Welding is looking for three skilled tradespeople to join our team in Inverell, working across heavy fabrication, welding and specialist equipment.
This is not production-line work. You'll be working on large, heavy apparatus and projects where no two days are necessarily the same — including crane grillages, earth-moving equipment, vacuum trucks and mobile welding work.
We're looking for people who want more than just their next job. This is a long-term career opportunity with a well-established business that values people who take pride in their work, have a good attitude and are willing to go the extra mile.
About the roleYou'll work across a range of heavy fabrication and welding projects, including:
  • Heavy structural and general fabrication
  • Welding and fabrication of crane-related equipment and grillages
  • Earth-moving equipment
  • Vacuum trucks and specialist heavy equipment
  • Mobile welding and field-based work
  • Working with a range of materials and fabrication requirements
The standard working week is 38 hours, with overtime available. Typical hours are 6.00am–4.30pm Monday to Thursday, with a shorter day on Friday. Weekend work is occasional rather than routine.
What we're looking forYou will have:
  • Certificate III or IV in Engineering – Fabrication Trade (Boilermaker/Welder or Metal Fabricator), or a closely related trade qualification.
  • Solid experience in heavy fabrication and welding
  • The ability to read and work from drawings
  • A strong focus on quality, safety and getting the job done properly
  • A practical, reliable and positive attitude
  • The ability to work independently as well as part of a team
Experience working with stainless steel and aluminium would be an advantage.
A crane licence and/or forklift licence would also be beneficial, but these are not essential.
Most importantly, we're looking for people who are reliable, take pride in their work and want to build something long term. APS Welding is prepared to invest in the right people who demonstrate commitment and a willingness to learn and contribute.
Why join APS Welding?
  • $35–$50 per hour (open to negotiation - tell us what you're worth!), depending on experience
  • 38-hour standard week plus overtime
  • Varied, interesting heavy fabrication work — not production line
  • Long-term career opportunity and strong job security
  • Opportunity to develop your skills across different types of equipment and projects
  • A business that values and invests in people who go the extra mile
  • Occasional rather than regular weekend work
  • Immediate start
  • Relocation support may be available for the right candidate
Thinking about relocating to Inverell?If you're interested in the opportunity but aren't ready to commit to a move straight away, APS Welding can offer a trial period. Come to Inverell, work with the team and experience the job and the area before making a longer-term decision.
For the right person, this could be the start of a long-term career and a new lifestyle in regional NSW.
If you're a qualified tradesperson who enjoys working with big equipment, solving practical problems and producing quality work, we'd like to hear from you.

For a confidential call, please call Mary Butler, 02 6691 9102

job.title: Change and Implementation Officer
job.description:
Chandler Macleod is recruiting on behalf of our client for an experienced Change and Implementation Officer to support the successful delivery of a significant organisational transformation program.

This role will lead change management, communications, training, business readiness and implementation activities across multiple workstreams. Working closely with senior leaders, project teams and business stakeholders, you will help prepare the organisation for change, drive adoption of new processes and systems, and ensure sustainable business outcomes.

This opportunity is ideal for a change professional who thrives in complex environments, enjoys engaging stakeholders at all levels and has a strong track record delivering successful change and implementation initiatives.

About the Role In this position, you will:

  • Develop and deliver integrated change and implementation plans across multiple workstreams.
  • Assess the impact of process and system changes on employees, teams and ways of working.
  • Lead stakeholder engagement, consultation and communication activities.
  • Design and coordinate training programs, support materials and user guidance.
  • Conduct business readiness assessments and identify adoption risks.
  • Support implementation activities and provide early-life operational support.
  • Monitor adoption, stakeholder feedback and business outcomes following implementation.
  • Develop procedures, templates and support documentation to enable long-term business ownership.
  • Work closely with project teams and senior stakeholders to deliver successful organisational change outcomes.
Key Criteria to be Successful To be successful in this role, you will demonstrate:

  • Extensive experience delivering change management, implementation or business adoption initiatives within complex organisations.
  • Proven ability to assess organisational impacts and support stakeholders through change.
  • Experience developing and delivering communication, consultation, engagement and training strategies.
  • Strong capability in business readiness assessment, risk identification and implementation planning.
  • Excellent stakeholder management skills with the ability to influence and build trusted relationships at all levels.
  • Highly developed written and verbal communication skills, including preparing communications, briefing materials and training content.
  • Strong planning, organisation and problem-solving skills with the ability to manage multiple priorities and workstreams.
  • Relevant qualifications or significant equivalent experience in change management, organisational development, communications, learning or a related discipline.
Desirable Experience
  • Experience supporting enterprise-wide process, policy, finance or technology transformation programs.
  • Familiarity with structured change methodologies such as Prosci ADKAR, Kotter or similar frameworks.
  • Experience working within government, public sector or purpose-driven organisations.
  • Exposure to complex business transformation, systems implementation or operational improvement programs.
If you are an experienced change professional with a passion for stakeholder engagement, organisational transformation and delivering lasting business improvements, we encourage you to apply.

job.title: Showroom Concierge
job.description:
Bayswater | Monday to Friday | 9:00am – 5:00pm
Immediate annual leave cover: 30 September – 9 October
Plus ongoing ad hoc and short-notice opportunities

Are you someone who can answer a busy phone, acknowledge a customer walking through the door and keep things moving without appearing flustered?

Chandler Macleod is seeking a polished and professional Showroom Concierge to provide front-of-house support within an established Melbourne-based manufacturer and supplier servicing the building, renovation and interior design space.

Based within a beautifully presented showroom in Bayswater, this role is more than traditional reception. You’ll be the first point of contact for customers, trades and visitors while also managing a busy phone line, directing enquiries and supporting the wider sales, logistics and administration teams.

We are initially recruiting for annual leave cover from 30 September to 9 October, however we are also looking to build a small pool of reliable Showroom Concierges who are interested in ongoing casual, ad hoc and short-notice assignments.

About the role
Sitting front-of-house within the showroom, you’ll help create a professional and welcoming experience while keeping day-to-day enquiries moving efficiently.

Your responsibilities will include:
  • Meeting and greeting customers, visitors and trades entering the showroom
  • Managing a high volume of incoming calls and directing enquiries to sales, logistics and administration teams
  • Acknowledging and assisting customers while balancing phone and administrative priorities
  • Coordinating customer collections and obtaining relevant sign-offs
  • Entering and updating information across internal systems
  • Using Monday.com for lead and pipeline management
  • Using SAP in relation to production orders
  • Providing general front-of-house and administrative support to the wider team
  • Maintaining a professional, organised and composed showroom environment

About you
We’re looking for someone who understands that great front-of-house service is about more than simply being friendly.

You’ll know how to read the room, communicate professionally and remain composed when several things are happening at once. You can warmly acknowledge a customer while you’re on the phone, prioritise what needs your attention and work alongside a busy team without disrupting their workflow.

You’ll ideally bring:
  • Previous experience in reception, concierge, showroom, customer service or administration
  • A polished and confident phone manner
  • Strong verbal communication and professional presentation
  • The ability to manage competing priorities without becoming visibly overwhelmed
  • Good judgement and an understanding of professional workplace etiquette
  • A considerate, team-focused approach
  • Confidence learning new systems and processes
  • Reliable attendance and strong punctuality

Experience with Monday.com or SAP would be advantageous but is not essential.

An interest in interior design, architecture, home renovations, building products or property would also be well suited to the showroom environment.

Looking for flexible or ad hoc work?We’d also love to hear from experienced reception, concierge and customer service professionals interested in joining our casual relief pool.

These opportunities are suited to candidates who may be available for planned annual leave cover as well as occasional same-day or short-notice assignments when a client requires unexpected reception or showroom coverage.

You’ll complete our onboarding requirements in advance so that, when suitable work becomes available, we can contact you directly regarding the assignment.

If you’re reliable, professional and enjoy stepping into different workplaces and getting up to speed quickly, this could be a great way to pick up additional casual work throughout the year.

Apply now to be considered for the upcoming Bayswater assignment and future casual opportunities with Chandler Macleod.

job.title: Production Supervisor or Manager
job.description:
Production Supervisor / Production ManagerAPS Welding | Inverell, NSW
Permanent, full-time | $120K-$150K + super (negotiable depending on experience) | Immediate start
APS Welding is looking for an experienced Production Supervisor or Production Manager to join our team in Inverell.
This is a newly created role and an opportunity to have a real influence on how our workshop operates as the business continues to grow.
We're looking for someone who can bring strong practical production experience, attention to detail and the ability to lead people well. Depending on your experience and capability, the role could be suited to someone ready to step into a Production Supervisor position or an experienced Production Manager looking for a hands-on regional opportunity.
About the roleYou'll take responsibility for helping keep jobs moving efficiently through the workshop, while working closely with clients, suppliers and the APS Welding team.
Your responsibilities will include:
  • Managing and coordinating production activities across the workshop
  • Directing and supporting the fabrication and welding team
  • Managing jobs from commencement through to completion
  • Liaising with clients and understanding their requirements
  • Assisting with quoting and estimating
  • Reading and interpreting engineering and fabrication drawings
  • Supporting procurement and ensuring materials and equipment are available when required
  • Monitoring quality and managing non-conformances
  • Supporting recruitment and helping shape and restructure the team as the business grows
  • Managing attendance, safety compliance and day-to-day workforce requirements
  • Identifying opportunities to improve workshop efficiency and ways of working
  • Working closely with the team to maintain high standards of safety, quality and customer service
What we're looking forIdeally, you'll have:
  • Experience supervising or managing a fabrication, engineering, manufacturing or similar production environment
  • A trade qualification, ideally in Boilermaking, Fabrication, Welding or a related engineering trade, is strongly preferred
  • Experience reading and interpreting technical and engineering drawings
  • Experience managing people and coordinating a busy workshop
  • A practical understanding of production planning, quality and procurement
  • Experience dealing with workplace safety, and resolving issues
  • Strong attention to detail
  • A strong commitment to workplace safety and compliance
  • Good communication skills and the confidence to deal directly with clients
  • A hands-on, practical approach and the ability to make decisions
Experience with heavy fabrication, cranes, earth-moving equipment, vacuum trucks or similar heavy equipment would be highly regarded.
More than just managing productionWe're a harmonious team, and that matters to us.
We want people to enjoy coming to work and to be proud of what they produce. The person in this role will play an important part in maintaining that culture while ensuring the workshop is organised, productive and operating safely.
We're looking for someone who can lead rather than simply supervise — someone who is comfortable getting involved, supporting the team, dealing with issues as they arise and helping people perform at their best.
The working weekThis is a permanent, full-time position with a standard 38-hour week.
Typical hours are 6.00am–4.30pm Monday to Thursday, with a shorter six-hour day on Friday.
The Production Supervisor/Manager needs to be available for the hours the workshop is operating, with only occasional weekend work. Weekend requirements would typically be no more than a half day.
Why join APS Welding?
  • Permanent, long-term career opportunity
  • $120K-$150K + super, negotiable depending on experience
  • Overtime available
  • Newly created role with genuine opportunity to make an impact
  • Varied heavy fabrication and specialist equipment work
  • Strong job security
  • Friendly, harmonious team environment
  • Opportunity to help shape and develop the production team
  • Immediate start
  • Relocation support may be available for the right candidate

job.title: Client Relations & Hire Specialist
job.description:
We are seeking a commercially minded and personable Client Relations & Hire Specialist to join an established plant and equipment hire business based in Dandenong South.

This is a hands-on, phone-based role focused on maintaining strong client relationships and generating dry hire opportunities across the civil and construction industries.

A large part of your day will involve proactively contacting existing and previous clients, keeping the business front of mind and understanding their upcoming projects and equipment requirements. You'll also manage inbound hire enquiries, prepare and follow up quotes, re-engage dormant clients and identify opportunities to develop new business.

There is a genuine sales element to the role, so you'll need to be comfortable picking up the phone, starting conversations and asking for the business. However, this isn't a traditional BDM position focused solely on cold acquisition or being out on the road.

Working within a small, close-knit team, you'll also be someone who is happy to jump in and assist with incoming calls and general client enquiries when needed.


Key Responsibilities
  • Proactively contact existing, previous and prospective clients to generate hire opportunities
  • Build and maintain relationships with clients across the civil and construction sectors
  • Re-engage dormant clients and identify upcoming projects or equipment requirements
  • Manage inbound hire enquiries via phone and email
  • Prepare quotes and proactively follow up outstanding opportunities
  • Identify and approach prospective clients where appropriate
  • Promote available equipment to maximise fleet utilisation
  • Maintain accurate client and sales activity within HubSpot CRM
  • Assist with incoming calls and general client enquiries across the office when required
  • Conduct phone and Microsoft Teams meetings, with occasional site visits where beneficial
  • Work closely with the wider team to maintain client engagement and sales momentum

About You
We're looking for someone who genuinely enjoys speaking with clients and is comfortable with the commercial side of relationship building.
You'll ideally be:
  • Confident making proactive outbound calls and asking clients about upcoming requirements
  • Personable, genuine and able to build rapport quickly
  • Commercially minded and comfortable identifying sales opportunities
  • Comfortable approaching new clients as well as working with established relationships
  • Persistent with follow-ups without being overly pushy
  • Reliable, consistent and willing to get involved wherever needed
  • Organised and disciplined with quotes, follow-ups and CRM activity
  • Comfortable working autonomously within a small office environment
  • Looking for a stable, long-term opportunity where you can become a valued part of the team

Experience within plant and equipment hire, earthmoving, civil construction, construction or a related industry will be highly regarded. Strong internal sales, hire or client relationship experience from another industry will also be considered.


What's on Offer
  • $80,000–$85,000 + super
  • Permanent, full-time opportunity
  • Dandenong South location
  • 100% office-based, with occasional site visits
  • Small, close-knit and down-to-earth team
  • Established client relationships to build upon
  • A varied mix of client relationships, hire coordination and proactive sales
  • Stable, long-term opportunity within an established business

job.description:

This role will play a key part in shaping and governing enterprise security architecture across complex IT and Operational Technology (OT) environments, ensuring security is embedded into technology strategy, solution design, and delivery initiatives.

You will partner with technology, architecture, cyber security, risk, and project teams to deliver secure-by-design solutions aligned with business objectives and industry best practices.

This is an excellent opportunity for someone who enjoys influencing enterprise-wide security outcomes, driving security maturity, and working across a diverse technology landscape.

  • Develop and maintain security architecture standards, principles, patterns, and reference architectures.
  • Provide expert security architecture guidance across cloud, hybrid, on-premises, and OT environments.
  • Conduct security architecture reviews for major programs and technology initiatives.

    • Identity & Access Management (IAM)
    • Network Security
    • Application Security
    • Data Protection
    • Security Monitoring
    • Zero Trust Architectures

  • Partner with enterprise architects, project teams, cyber security specialists, and business stakeholders to embed security throughout the delivery lifecycle.

  • Proven experience in a Security Architect role within large and complex enterprise environments.
  • Strong understanding of security architecture frameworks such as:
    • SABSA

  • Extensive experience designing secure architectures across:

job.title: Learning Design Specialist
job.description:
Primary purpose The role is responsible for creating engaging content for learning initiatives and delivery using a variety of learning creation tools and platforms delivered via blended learning methodologies.

This will be achieved via direct and indirect consultation with the branch Clients, industry and Strategy teams, and be developed to ensure relevant regulatory standards are adhered and followed in conjunction with client specific requirements, including both soft skills and hard skills.

Key accountabilities
• Create engaging, high quality and compelling course content and artefacts that meet the required needs of our clients.
• Engage with clients to identify specific learning outcomes and or requirements inclusive of delivery methods, content type and regulatory and legislative outcomes or requirements.
• Use Learning and Assessment Strategies (LAS), story boards and supporting artefacts to create detailed course content for varied audiences cover a broad range of learning levels.

Role Description 

• Create supporting learning material such as audio, video, simulations, work instructions, quick reference guides, role plays, games etc. that align to client objectives.
• Build engaging exercises and course content that enhances the learning experience.
• Design assessment tools that appropriately measure learner competencies, including but not limited to knowledge and skills.
• Ensure training artefacts developed are in line with the required and or agreed standards/regulations and where applicable develop learning content that meet the compliance standards as outlined within the relevant VET Standards and or Regulatory requirements.

Key challenges

Chandler Macleod is seeking a trade-qualified Fitter to join an established industry leader specialising in truck-mounted cranes and mobile lifting solutions.

While a Mechanical Fitter or Fitter and Turner is preferred, applications are also welcomed from Heavy Vehicle Mechanics, Plant Mechanics and Boilermakers with strong mechanical aptitude and a willingness to learn.

Working within a close-knit workshop team, you will primarily assist with assembling new truck-mounted cranes, along with maintenance and service work.

Tradespeople generally work collaboratively in small teams, with everyone contributing across the broader manufacturing and assembly process. You won’t be restricted to one discipline—the team is looking for someone open-minded, adaptable and willing to assist wherever needed.

  • A flexible attitude and willingness to contribute across all areas of the workshop
  • A team-focused approach and strong work ethic
  • A commitment to quality workmanship and safe work practices

What’s on Offer
  • Permanent, stable employment with OT available

  • Opportunities to become multi-skilled across crane assembly, fitting, fabrication, and servicing
  • Supportive team environment with exceptional employee tenure

job.title: Project Manager (Specialist Projects)
job.description:
Project Manager (Specialist Projects)
Kurri Kurri, NSW
Attractive Salary Package

Our client is seeking an experienced and results-driven Project Manager to join their Project Delivery team based in Kurri Kurri, NSW.

This is an exciting opportunity to lead a diverse portfolio of sustaining and capital projects across mobile delivery systems, infrastructure upgrades, commissioning activities, asset mobilisation, and operational improvement initiatives.

About the Role Reporting to the Lead Projects, you will be responsible for the end-to-end delivery of multiple projects, ensuring outcomes are achieved safely, on time, within budget, and to the highest standards.

Key responsibilities include:

  • Managing multiple sustaining and capital projects simultaneously.
  • Developing project scopes, schedules, budgets, and risk management plans.
  • Coordinating contractors, suppliers, procurement activities, and project resources.
  • Managing project governance, reporting, forecasting, and project controls.
  • Leading mobilisation, construction, commissioning, and handover activities.
  • Building strong relationships with internal and external stakeholders.
  • Ensuring compliance with safety, environmental, and regulatory requirements.
  • Driving projects through to successful completion while balancing competing priorities.
About You
We are looking for a practical project professional with a strong delivery focus and the ability to navigate complexity.

You may come from a background in:
  • Project Delivery
  • Mining
  • Fixed Plant or Mobile Equipment
  • Civil Construction
  • Heavy Manufacturing
  • Maintenance and Shutdowns
  • Operations or Logistics
  • Trades or Construction Supervision
While engineering qualifications may be beneficial, this is not a design engineering role. We are particularly interested in candidates who have successfully coordinated and delivered projects within operational, maintenance, construction, or manufacturing environments. Formal project management qualifications will be highly regarded.

What Will Make You Successful

The ideal candidate will:
  • Make sound decisions with incomplete information.
  • Thrive in ambiguous and changing environments.
  • Balance competing stakeholder expectations.
  • Drive outcomes despite uncertainty.
  • Maintain strong ownership and accountability.
  • Be highly organised and capable of managing multiple projects concurrently.
  • Hold stakeholders accountable and follow through on commitments.
  • Focus on delivering practical outcomes rather than pursuing technical perfection.
In short, we're looking for someone who can bring structure to complexity, coordinate multiple stakeholders, and consistently deliver successful project outcomes.

Key Requirements
  • 5+ years' experience managing capital and/or sustaining projects.
  • Qualifications in Project Management, Engineering, Construction, or equivalent industry experience.
  • Strong contractor management and stakeholder engagement skills.
  • Demonstrated experience managing project budgets, schedules, and risk.
  • Excellent communication, planning, and organisational skills.
  • Experience working within industrial, manufacturing, mining, maintenance, or construction environments.
What's on Offer
  • Attractive salary package.
  • Opportunity to manage a diverse portfolio of projects with significant business impact.
  • Supportive and collaborative project delivery environment.
  • Minimal travel requirements (less than 10%).
  • Based in Kurri Kurri, NSW.
If you're a proactive Project Manager who enjoys creating order from complexity, influencing stakeholders, and delivering outcomes, we'd love to hear from you. Apply today for a confidential discussion.

job.title: Production Operator
job.description:
Production Operator
We are seeking reliable and motivated Production Operator to join our manufacturing client based in Beverley. This is a hands-on role working within a production environment, supporting the efficient operation of the product fill line and maintaining high-quality standards.
This position offers a Monday to Friday roster, with rotating day and afternoon shifts. Occasional weekend work may be required to meet production demands. You'll rotate through a variety of production tasks, providing plenty of variety throughout your workday while contributing to a safe and productive workplace.
 
Key Responsibilities
  • Rotate through various production and fill line tasks
  • Load buckets and lids onto the production line
  • Connect hoses and fill heads to support filling operations
  • Operate control panels and production equipment
  • Stack, wrap and prepare pallets for dispatch
  • Move raw materials and finished products throughout the site
  • Operate forklifts and other mobile plant equipment where licensed
  • Perform routine cleaning and housekeeping duties
  • Follow quality, safety and operational procedures at all times
About You
  • Previous experience in manufacturing, production, process work or machine operation is highly regarded
  • Comfortable working in a fast-paced environment
  • Physically fit and capable of manual handling tasks
  • Strong attention to detail and commitment to quality
  • Reliable, punctual and safety-focused
  • Able to work effectively as part of a team
  • Forklift licence is advantageous but not essential
Requirements
  • Full working rights within Australia
  • Availability to work rotating day and afternoon shifts between 6:00am and 8:45pm
  • Current driver's licence and reliable transport
  • Ability to pass a National Police Check
  • Ability to pass a pre-employment Drug and Alcohol Screen
What's on Offer?
  • Immediate start available
  • Competitive casual hourly rate of $46 per hour + penalties 
  • Full-time hours with rotating shifts
  • Variety of duties through regular task rotation
  • Supportive team environment
  • Potential for ongoing or permanent employment for suitable candidates
How to Apply
If you're looking for your next opportunity within the manufacturing industry and enjoy hands-on work in a team-focused environment, click APPLY NOW and submit your resume.
