job.description:
Chandler Macleod is recruiting on behalf of our client for multiple Business Support Officer opportunities. This is a rewarding role where you'll play an important part in supporting participants through key stages of their journey, delivering quality customer service and helping to achieve positive outcomes.
Working within a collaborative and fast-paced environment, you will manage a variety of administrative, operational and customer-focused tasks while engaging with participants, providers and stakeholders across Australia. This a full time, office based, labour hire contract.

About the Role As a Participant Support Officer, you'll be responsible for managing a diverse workload, resolving enquiries, and supporting participants through established processes and pathways. You'll use a range of systems and tools to review information, assess participant matters, and ensure actions are completed accurately and within required timeframes.

This role requires strong judgement, empathy, attention to detail and the ability to communicate effectively with people from diverse backgrounds.

Key Responsibilities
  • Manage participant-related enquiries and provide accurate information and support.
  • Conduct reviews of participant information and maintain records across multiple systems.
  • Make outbound calls to participants, providers and stakeholders to gather information and progress matters.
  • Assess and action participant requests in line with legislation, policies and operational guidelines.
  • Escalate complex issues where required and contribute to achieving team service delivery outcomes.
  • Assist with process improvements, reporting activities and project-related initiatives.
  • Work collaboratively with team members to share knowledge, provide feedback and support continuous improvement.
About You To be successful in this role, you will demonstrate:
  • Exceptional communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to build rapport and engage with a broad range of stakeholders.
  • Strong customer service experience within a high-volume environment.
  • The ability to remain calm, professional and solution-focused when dealing with sensitive or complex situations.
  • Excellent organisational skills and the ability to manage competing priorities.
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving capabilities.
  • A high level of attention to detail when working with data and documentation.
  • Experience interpreting policies, procedures or legislative frameworks.
  • Confidence using Microsoft Office and navigating multiple systems simultaneously.
What We're Looking For
  • Experience in administration, customer service, contact centres, case management, human services, health, government or community services environments.
  • Ability to handle sensitive information with professionalism and confidentiality.
  • Demonstrated resilience, adaptability and commitment to delivering positive customer outcomes.
  • A collaborative team player with a proactive approach to learning and continuous improvement.
For any queries, please contact volumefedgov@chandlermacleod.com

If you match the above criteria APPLY now 

At Chandler Macleod, we are committed to fostering a diverse workforce where everyone is welcome. We encourage applications from Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples, women, neurodiverse, people living with a disability and the LGBTIQA+ community.

You can read more about our commitment to diversity and inclusion at https://www.chandlermacleod.com/diversity-and-inclusion.

job.title: Support Needs Assessors
job.description:
Chandler Macleod is seeking experienced Support Needs Assessors to join a Federal Government client on a full-time contract. In this role, you will deliver high-quality, person-centred assessments, working directly with participants to identify and articulate their support needs in a clear, evidence-based and respectful manner.

Key Responsibilities
  • Conduct support needs assessments with participants and their representatives
  • Analyse information and external evidence to support sound, evidence-based decisions
  • Prepare clear, accurate assessment reports
  • Communicate assessment processes and outcomes clearly (virtual and face-to-face)
  • Apply relevant policies, procedures and legislative frameworks
  • Identify and escalate complex or high-risk matters
  • Collaborate with internal stakeholders to support participant outcomes
  • Maintain accurate records using case management systems
  • Adapt assessment approaches to suit individual participant needs
About You You will bring:

  • Strong communication and stakeholder engagement skills
  • Experience in assessment, interviewing or case management
  • Ability to interpret evidence and provide clear, defensible recommendations
  • A commitment to person-centred, inclusive and trauma-informed practice
  • Sound judgement, professionalism and ethical integrity
  • Ability to manage competing priorities and deadlines
  • Experience working within or knowledge of NDIS or similar frameworks (highly regarded)
Essential Requirements
  • Recognised tertiary qualification in a relevant discipline, such as:

    • Occupational Therapy, Physiotherapy, Speech Pathology
    • Social Work, Counselling, Psychology/Psychotherapy
    • Exercise Physiology, Dietetics, Rehabilitation Counselling
    • Nursing (RN/EN), Education-qualified clinicians
    • NDIS Behaviour Support Practitioner
  • Experience in support needs assessments or similar frameworks

  • Understanding of person-centred and strengths-based approaches

For any queries, please contact volumefedgov@chandlermacleod.com 

If you fit the above criteria we would love to hear from you, APPLY now!

job.title: Group Finance Manager
job.description:
Group Finance Manager, Multi-Entity Private Group
Campbelfield 

Our client is a privately owned, founder-led group of businesses with a combined annual turnover exceeding $30 million. The Group spans six operating entities across bin hire and property development, waste services, legal services, agriculture and wellness, all wholly owned by a single Director who moves fast and runs multiple projects at once.

This is not a conventional Group Finance Manager role. It's a genuine seat at the table with a founder who has built serious value across his businesses but knows his financial oversight hasn't kept pace with growth. Fund flows between entities haven't always been formally documented, and there's currently no single consolidated view of the Group's debt, cash or net asset position.

You'll be the first person to sit across the entire Group with a clear mandate: bring order, structure and visibility to the Director's complete financial position, business and personal.

Responsibilities
  • Owning the Group's consolidated financial position at all times, with the Director able to get an accurate answer to any financial question within the hour
  • Managing everything from personal expenses through to major capital requirements for property acquisitions and construction
  • Rolling cash flow forecasts and a weekly cash and debt summary for the Director
  • Overseeing the bookkeeping team and liaising with the external tax agent on compliance
  • Building and enforcing clear financial controls, including a formal intercompany transfer process
  • Supporting evaluation of new property acquisitions, including development feasibility modelling
  • Managing banking relationships and lender communication across a large number of accounts
What We're Looking For:
  • 7+ years in a senior finance role, ideally across multiple entities or a group structure
  • Comfortable working directly with a founder where priorities shift fast; you're a stabilising force, not an extra variable
  • Advanced Xero skills across multiple entities, without needing support
  • Experience managing or directing bookkeepers and junior finance staff
  • CPA or CA preferred, though exceptional experience will be considered in place of it
  • Absolute discretion; you'll have full visibility of the Director's personal and business financial position
Why This Role:

 At 30 days, you'll have delivered a complete financial map of the Group. At 6 months, clear controls are in place and the Director gets a weekly summary he can rely on. At 12 months, you're his most trusted operational partner, contributing directly to decisions on acquisitions, cash deployment and growth.

This is a genuinely broad, high-trust mandate for someone who wants ownership, not just oversight.

To apply, submit your CV along with a short cover note on why this particular role, its pace, complexity and scope, appeals to you.

job.title: Catering Attendant EOI
job.description:
Chandler Macleod is seeking Expressions of Interest from reliable, hardworking Catering Attendants / Potwash to support our client’s industrial catering team based in Adelaide’s western suburbs.

These opportunities may suit people looking for ongoing and regular work in a clean, inclusive onsite environment, with onsite parking, full uniform, and meals provided.

Key responsibilities
  • Sorting and packing catering equipment
  • Fast-paced food preparation and meal plating
  • Repetitive manual handling and packing duties
  • General cleaning and hygiene tasks
  • Washing/cleaning equipment including cutlery and dishes
To be considered, you will ideally have
  • Recent, relevant experience in food manufacturing / high-volume food environments
  • Strong knowledge of food hygiene practices and quality standards
  • Good literacy and numeracy skills
  • Ability to pass a full medical and National Police Clearance
  • Flexibility to work day and afternoon shifts across a 7-day roster
  • Reliable car and licence
  • Full working rights and strong availability
  • Proven reliability, initiative, and strong work ethic
Important: This role does not count towards the 88 days requirement for a Working Holiday Visa.

How to register your interest If you’re available for an immediate start and would like to be considered as shifts become available, please click APPLY NOW and upload your resume. A consultant will be in touch after reviewing your application.

You can read more about our commitment to diversity and inclusion at https://www.chandlermacleod.com/diversity-and-inclusion.

job.title: Business Support Officer
job.description:
Chandler Macleod is recruiting on behalf of our client for multiple Business Support Officer opportunities. This is a rewarding role where you'll play an important part in supporting participants through key stages of their journey, delivering quality customer service and helping to achieve positive outcomes.
Working within a collaborative and fast-paced environment, you will manage a variety of administrative, operational and customer-focused tasks while engaging with participants, providers and stakeholders across Australia. This a full time, office based, labour hire contract.

About the Role As a Participant Support Officer, you'll be responsible for managing a diverse workload, resolving enquiries, and supporting participants through established processes and pathways. You'll use a range of systems and tools to review information, assess participant matters, and ensure actions are completed accurately and within required timeframes.

This role requires strong judgement, empathy, attention to detail and the ability to communicate effectively with people from diverse backgrounds.

Key Responsibilities
  • Manage participant-related enquiries and provide accurate information and support.
  • Conduct reviews of participant information and maintain records across multiple systems.
  • Make outbound calls to participants, providers and stakeholders to gather information and progress matters.
  • Assess and action participant requests in line with legislation, policies and operational guidelines.
  • Escalate complex issues where required and contribute to achieving team service delivery outcomes.
  • Assist with process improvements, reporting activities and project-related initiatives.
  • Work collaboratively with team members to share knowledge, provide feedback and support continuous improvement.
About You To be successful in this role, you will demonstrate:
  • Exceptional communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to build rapport and engage with a broad range of stakeholders.
  • Strong customer service experience within a high-volume environment.
  • The ability to remain calm, professional and solution-focused when dealing with sensitive or complex situations.
  • Excellent organisational skills and the ability to manage competing priorities.
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving capabilities.
  • A high level of attention to detail when working with data and documentation.
  • Experience interpreting policies, procedures or legislative frameworks.
  • Confidence using Microsoft Office and navigating multiple systems simultaneously.
What We're Looking For
  • Experience in administration, customer service, contact centres, case management, human services, health, government or community services environments.
  • Ability to handle sensitive information with professionalism and confidentiality.
  • Demonstrated resilience, adaptability and commitment to delivering positive customer outcomes.
  • A collaborative team player with a proactive approach to learning and continuous improvement.
For any queries, please contact volumefedgov@chandlermacleod.com

job.title: Branch Manager
job.description:
Branch Manager | Canberra | FMCG & Distribution

Permanent | Full time

$165,000 – $175,000 + super | STI | Fully Maintained Company Vehicle
  • Senior leadership opportunity within a well-established national business
  • Lead a 50–60 person branch operation
  • Responsibility across sales, operations, transport, warehouse and customer service
  • Potential relocation assistance for the right candidate
The Opportunity

We are seeking an experienced Branch Manager to take overall responsibility for a large and established distribution operation in Canberra.

This is a senior leadership position with responsibility across sales, operations, transport, warehouse, administration and customer service, with a strong focus on branch profitability, customer service and team performance.

Reporting to senior management, you'll lead a team of approximately 50–60 employees and work closely with an experienced leadership group across the branch.

This is an opportunity for a confident and commercially minded leader to take ownership of an established operation, drive performance and identify opportunities to improve the way the business operates.

About the Role

You'll be responsible for:
  • Leading the day-to-day operations of the branch across sales, warehouse, transport and administration.
  • Delivering budgeted EBIT, revenue and profitability targets.
  • Managing branch budgets, forecasts, costs and financial performance.
  • Analysing P&L results and operational KPIs and taking corrective action where required.
  • Leading and developing a team of approximately 50–60 employees.
  • Driving customer growth, retention and service excellence.
  • Building strong relationships with customers, suppliers and internal stakeholders.
  • Managing inventory and ensuring customer demand is supported effectively.
  • Identifying new business opportunities and opportunities for growth.
  • Improving productivity, processes and operational efficiency.
  • Ensuring high standards of WHS, food safety, HACCP and Chain of Responsibility compliance.
  • Creating a culture of accountability, teamwork and continuous improvement.
  • Making timely decisions and providing clear direction across the branch.
About You

We're looking for an experienced operational leader who combines commercial understanding with strong people and operational leadership.

You'll ideally have:
  • Previous experience as a Branch Manager, Operations Manager, Distribution Manager, General Manager or similar.
  • Experience managing a sizeable workforce and multiple operational functions.
  • Strong commercial acumen and the ability to interpret P&L, budgets and financial performance.
  • Experience managing costs, productivity and operational KPIs.
  • Strong customer relationship and stakeholder management skills.
  • Excellent problem-solving and decision-making ability.
  • A visible, hands-on leadership style.
  • The confidence to challenge existing processes and drive positive change.
  • Strong communication and people management skills.
  • The ability to perform in a fast-paced, operational environment.
Experience in these areas will be highly regarded:
  • FMCG
  • Food distribution or foodservice
  • Grocery or wholesale distribution
  • Transport and logistics
  • Warehouse and distribution
  • High-volume operational environments
  • HACCP and food safety
  • Chain of Responsibility
  • WHS and psychosocial safety
Forklift or heavy vehicle licences are advantageous but not essential.

The Leadership Opportunity

This role will suit someone who enjoys being close to the operation and isn't afraid to make decisions.

You'll be taking over an established operation with experienced people and established ways of working.

The opportunity is to build on what's working, identify what can be improved and lead the team through positive change.

We're looking for someone who:
  • Takes ownership
  • Leads from the front
  • Makes decisions
  • Holds people accountable
  • Develops and supports their team
  • Builds strong customer relationships
  • Looks for better ways of doing things
  • Can balance people, customers and commercial outcomes
What's on Offer
  • $165,000 – $175,000 + super
  • Fully maintained company vehicle
  • STI / incentive program
  • Potential relocation assistance for the right candidate
  • Staff discounts and additional benefits
  • Opportunity to lead a substantial operation within an established national business
  • Genuine scope to influence operational performance and branch growth
Apply Now

If you're an experienced Branch or Operations Manager looking for a role where you can take genuine ownership and make a measurable impact, we'd like to hear from you.

Apply now with your updated resume and cover letter.

Early applications are encouraged, as shortlisting may commence before the closing date of Friday 2 October 2026.

Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted. All applications will be treated confidentially.

As part of the recruitment process, successful candidates may be required to complete employment checks, which may include a medical assessment, drug and alcohol testing, National Police History Check and licence validation.

At Chandler Macleod, we are committed to fostering a diverse workforce where everyone is welcome. We encourage applications from Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples, women, neurodiverse, people living with a disability and the LGBTIQA+ community.

You can read more about our commitment to diversity and inclusion at https://www.chandlermacleod.com/diversity-and-inclusion.

job.description:

As the Senior Project Manager, you will lead the end-to-end delivery of complex technology, OT, infrastructure, and cyber-related initiatives, ensuring successful outcomes across scope, schedule, budget, quality, risk, and business benefits. You are a confident and adaptable delivery professional who enjoys working in challenging environments and is comfortable balancing strategic oversight with detailed execution.
You will bring:

  • Strong communication and presentation skills, with the ability to simplify complex delivery issues and provide clear recommendations.

job.title: High Voltage Safety & Compliance Coordinator
job.description:
High Voltage Safety & Compliance Coordinator
Chadstone, VIC
$125,000 + 12% Superannuation
Permanent Full-Time
Onsite Position

Operating a purpose-built training facility, our client plays a vital role in developing apprentices, tradespeople and industry professionals across the energy, rail and major infrastructure sectors. Supporting training in power distribution, transmission and other critical industries, they are committed to maintaining a safe, compliant and industry-leading learning environment. Due to continued growth and operational requirements, an opportunity has become available for a High Voltage Safety & Compliance Coordinator to join their team at their Chadstone facility.

This is a unique opportunity for an experienced electrical professional to take ownership of safety, compliance and operational readiness across a specialised high-voltage training environment.
Working closely with trainers, contractors, industry stakeholders and safety teams, you will coordinate electrical safety systems, permits, inspections and maintenance activities while ensuring compliance with relevant legislation, regulations and industry standards.
In this role, you will play a key part in supporting the safe operation, maintenance and compliance of high-voltage and electrical training assets, helping to create a safe and effective environment for staff, students, apprentices and visitors.

Key Responsibilities
  • Coordinate the safe operation and use of high voltage and electrical training assets.
  • Administer and maintain permit-to-work systems, including Electrical Access Permits and excavation permits.
  • Maintain safety documentation including authorisations, competency records, inductions and compliance registers.
  • Coordinate planned and reactive maintenance activities across training infrastructure.
  • Manage inspections and ensure corrective actions and remediation works are completed.
  • Support ongoing compliance with Victorian electrical safety legislation, regulations and industry requirements.
  • Facilitate contractor and visitor inductions and ensure site compliance requirements are met.
  • Work collaboratively with trainers, operational teams and industry stakeholders to identify and manage risk.
  • Assist with the development, implementation and continuous improvement of safety management systems.
  • Liaise with regulatory bodies, contractors and industry partners as required.
  • Support a safe learning environment for apprentices, students, staff and visitors.
About You
To be successful in this role, you will bring:
  • Experience within electrical, utilities, infrastructure, energy or other high-risk operational environments.
  • Sound knowledge of electrical safety legislation, compliance requirements and safe work practices.
  • Experience managing permit systems, safety procedures and compliance documentation.
  • Knowledge of high voltage operations, switching, isolation procedures and access permit requirements.
  • Experience coordinating maintenance activities, inspections and risk management processes.
  • Strong stakeholder engagement and relationship management skills.
  • Excellent organisational, communication and record-keeping abilities.
  • A proactive and collaborative approach to safety and compliance.
Essential Requirements
  • Current ESI licence, electrical trade qualification or equivalent recognised qualification relevant to the role.
  • Demonstrated experience in electrical safety and compliance environments.
  • Strong knowledge of permit-to-work systems and safety management processes.
  • Valid Victorian Working with Children Check, or willingness to obtain one prior to commencement.
  • Full Australian working rights.
Desirable
  • Current or previous High Voltage Authorisation.
  • Experience within electricity distribution, transmission, rail, utilities or training environments.
  • Experience working with Energy Safe Victoria requirements or similar regulatory frameworks.
What's on Offer
  • $125,000 + 12% Superannuation.
  • Permanent full-time opportunity.
  • Stable, onsite role based in Chadstone.
  • Opportunity to work within a specialised high-voltage training environment.
  • Broad stakeholder engagement across industry, contractors and regulatory bodies.
  • Supportive and collaborative team culture.
  • A meaningful role helping develop the future workforce of Australia's energy and infrastructure sectors.
Additional Information
The successful candidate will be required to complete a National Police Check as part of the pre-employment process.

Asset Management
  • Lead a safety-driven and inclusive group
  • Frontline leadership position
  • 8:6 FIFO from Perth
  • Long Term Project
 
About the role:
We are seeking an engaging, safety and productivity focused Contractor Management Supervisor to join our Asset Management project team – focusing on town electrical infrastructure projects upgrading critical town infrastructure with voltages of up to 33kV. This role presents a fantastic opportunity to draw on your people leadership skills, coupled with your technical knowledge, to coordinate the safe execution of work in line with the project schedule. You will have a strong safety leadership focus ensuring the safe installation and commissioning of new electrical infrastructure within our Pilbara towns. This role is an excellent opportunity to showcase your influencing and stakeholder engagement skills. Working on an 8:6 FIFO roster and reporting to the Town EIR Project Manager for Asset Management.

  • Perform field verifications and interactions, displaying safety leadership
  • Ensure work management activities are undertaken in line with the SOW and RTIO work practices and procedures

  • Have previous experience working for Rio Tinto and managing sub-contractors (preferred)

In the Pilbara region of Western Australia, Rio Tinto owns a world-class, integrated network of 18 mines, 4 independent port terminals, a rail network spanning nearly 2,000 kilometres and related infrastructure – all designed to respond rapidly to changes in demand. Rio Tinto are one of the world’s leading producers and exporters of iron ore.

As a School Crossing Supervisor, you will play a vital role in keeping school-aged children, families, and pedestrians safe during busy morning and afternoon school times. This is a rewarding position where you’ll become a familiar and trusted face in your local community.

  • Be friendly, reliable, community-minded, and confident communicating with people of all ages
  • Be available for morning and/or afternoon shifts during school terms

We are looking for someone with strong practical laboratory experience who is comfortable taking ownership of day-to-day technical operations.
You will ideally bring:
  • Demonstrated experience working within chemistry, chemical engineering or a related laboratory environment
  • Extensive experience with the safe handling, transport and connection of compressed gas cylinders
  • Strong experience managing chemicals and chemical waste
  • Experience working with and maintaining specialised or custom chemical laboratory equipment
  • Previous laboratory operations and maintenance experience, ideally within a teaching or research environment
  • A sound understanding of OH&S legislation, laboratory safety requirements and relevant industry standards

  • Strong organisational skills with the ability to work autonomously and manage competing priorities

job.description:
Senior Investment Planning Analyst
Housing & Grid Infrastructure

Drive the planning and investment decisions that support Western Australia's future growth.

Our client is seeking an experienced Senior Investment Planning Analyst to play a key role in shaping major network infrastructure investment programs that support housing development, grid optimisation, and long-term network performance.

This is a highly visible position that combines strategic planning, portfolio management, financial forecasting, and stakeholder engagement. While advertised as a Senior Investment Planning Analyst, the successful candidate will operate as a Senior Grid Portfolio Analyst, responsible for developing investment plans, managing project pipelines, forecasting expenditure, and supporting critical network infrastructure programs.

About the Role
Working across large-scale housing and grid infrastructure portfolios, you will help ensure the right projects are planned, prioritised, funded, and delivered at the right time. You will provide valuable insights that support investment decisions, network capacity planning, and long-term infrastructure strategy.

This role offers the opportunity to work closely with planning, delivery, finance, and portfolio management teams while contributing to major infrastructure initiatives that support growing communities across Western Australia.

Key Responsibilities
Portfolio & Investment Planning
  • Develop and maintain short and long-term investment plans across housing and grid optimisation portfolios.
  • Build and manage multi-year project pipelines aligned with strategic network objectives.
  • Identify project dependencies, approval pathways, critical milestones, and delivery risks.
  • Support annual planning cycles and long-term network investment strategies.
Budgeting & Forecasting
  • Develop and maintain portfolio budgets and expenditure forecasts.
  • Translate capital investment plans into accurate monthly and annual financial forecasts.
  • Maintain rolling expenditure forecasts and analyse variances against budget.
  • Provide recommendations and insights to support investment decision-making.
Housing & Infrastructure Program Planning
  • Monitor infrastructure requirements associated with housing growth initiatives.
  • Analyse network capacity, anticipated housing developments, and energisation timelines.
  • Assess future investment requirements and identify potential capacity constraints.
  • Develop planning scenarios to support prioritisation and risk assessment.
Project Pipeline Management
  • Maintain a forward-looking portfolio of infrastructure projects.
  • Support resource planning, investment prioritisation, and governance processes.
  • Monitor project readiness and ensure key approvals are achieved within required timeframes.
  • Track delivery risks and emerging portfolio challenges.
Stakeholder Engagement & Reporting
  • Partner with cross-functional stakeholders across planning, delivery, finance, and portfolio teams.
  • Produce reports, forecasts, and analysis for senior leaders and decision-makers.
  • Develop tools, dashboards, and reporting processes that improve planning accuracy and visibility.
  • Drive continuous improvement initiatives across forecasting and portfolio management practices.
About You
  • Experience managing investment plans, project portfolios, infrastructure programs, or complex project schedules.
  • Strong financial modelling, budgeting, forecasting, and analytical capabilities.
  • The ability to interpret complex data and translate it into meaningful business insights.
  • Experience balancing multiple priorities, dependencies, resources, and delivery timelines.
  • Excellent stakeholder engagement and relationship-building skills.
  • Strong problem-solving skills with the ability to evaluate risks and provide practical recommendations.
  • Advanced Excel and data analysis capability, with experience using planning and reporting tools.
  • Experience within utilities, infrastructure, energy, transport, resources, or other asset-intensive environments highly regarded.
Why Apply? This is an opportunity to join a high-performing team where your work will directly influence major infrastructure investment decisions. You'll play a critical role in ensuring future housing developments and network infrastructure programs are supported by sound planning, robust forecasting, and effective portfolio management.

If you're an experienced portfolio, planning, or investment professional looking to make a meaningful impact on large-scale infrastructure programs, we would love to hear from you.

  • Maintain accurate inventory records and support stock control processes.
  • Uphold workplace health and safety procedures at all times.

  • Previous experience in a fast-paced production or feed mill environment preferred.

job.title: Production Chef
job.description:

$80,000–$88,000 pa (Pro Rata)
Perth Airport

Are you an experienced Chef with a passion for authentic flavours and high‑volume production? Join an airline catering team and play a key role in creating exceptional in‑flight meals enjoyed by passengers across the world.

Chandler Macleod is seeking Production Chefs who can bring expertise and consistency to our large‑scale client's airline food production operations.

About the Role
As an Airline Production Chef, you will prepare high‑quality dishes across a variety of Asian and Western cuisines — tailored for airline passengers in both Economy and Premium cabins. Working in a fast‑paced production kitchen, you’ll ensure every dish meets strict taste, presentation, and food‑safety standards.

This is initially a casual position (full-time hours) with annualised earnings ranging between $80K - $88K p/a. Permanent employment opportunities are considered following the successful completion of the first six months.  

Key Responsibilities
  • Prepare and cook authentic dishes in a bulk cooking production environment
  • Ensure consistency in taste, quality, portioning, and presentation
  • Maintain strict food‑safety compliance (HACCP and Airline Protocols)
  • Follow recipes for mass production without compromising flavour
  • Contribute to quality control and tasting sessions

What You’ll Bring
  • Certificate III or IV in Commercial Cookery or Trade Qualification in Australia
  • Minimum 5 years’ experience as a Chef
  • Experience in hot/cold meal production, batch cooking, and plated assembly
  • Understanding of airline catering operations and large‑scale food production
  • Strong attention to detail and ability to thrive in a fast‑paced environment
  • Great communication skills and the ability to work well in diverse teams
  • Flexibility to work both day and afternoon shifts including weekends and public holidays

Preferred Skills
  • Multilingual ability (Mandarin, Thai, Hindi, Japanese, etc.)

When you step into a role with our organisation, you become part of a truly global business committed to supporting your professional and personal success.

job.title: Senior Mechanical Engineer
job.description:

Wagerup, WA (Approximately 120km South of Perth) | Monday to Friday

This is an excellent opportunity for a technically strong engineering professional to provide leadership, drive reliability improvements, and mentor a small team of engineers within a complex processing environment.

Working closely with operations and maintenance teams, you will play a key role in ensuring equipment performance, asset integrity, and continuous improvement across critical plant areas.

As the Senior Mechanical Engineer, you will provide mechanical engineering leadership and technical expertise while leading a small team of engineers. You will be responsible for improving equipment reliability, supporting plant performance, and delivering engineering solutions that enhance operational efficiency and safety.
This opportunity is available from mid-September 2026 through to the end of January 2027 and offers a valuable leadership role within a large-scale refinery operation.

  • Provide mechanical engineering leadership and support across the Precipitation and Calcination areas.
  • Lead and facilitate problem-solving initiatives and Root Cause Analyses (RCA) for significant equipment failures and downtime events.
  • Provide expert engineering advice and technical support to operations and maintenance teams.
  • Develop and improve equipment management strategies using reliability engineering principles and methodologies.
  • Develop scopes of work for major equipment repairs and engineering projects, including fitness-for-service assessments.
  • Lead, coach and mentor a small engineering team, ensuring engineering outcomes are delivered safely and effectively.
  • Monitor, maintain and manage asset health and equipment performance.
  • Collaborate with stakeholders to identify continuous improvement opportunities and implement sustainable solutions.
About You

To be successful in this role, you will bring strong technical capability, leadership experience and a passion for reliability and asset management.

Essential Skills & Experience
  • Previous experience in a Senior or Lead Mechanical Engineering position.
  • Demonstrated experience leading or supervising a small engineering team.
  • Experience in maintenance, reliability, plant engineering and asset management.
  • Sound understanding of risk management, statutory compliance and reliability engineering principles.
  • Excellent communication and stakeholder engagement skills, with the ability to build relationships across all levels of an organisation.

job.title: Merchandiser - Portland
job.description:
Casual Merchandisers – Tip Top Bakeries | Portland

Chandler Macleod is seeking motivated individuals to join our team as Casual Merchandisers for our valued client, Tip Top Bakeries – Australia’s leading bakery products manufacturer.
These roles are available for an September start

About the Role
You’ll play a vital part in ensuring fresh bakery products are well-stocked, presented, and ready for customers in local supermarkets. This is a short term 6 week role with the potential to move into a permanent role with our client.

What We’re Looking For
✅ Own car and valid driver’s licence
✅ Approx. 10-15 hours per week
✅ Flexibility for additional shifts when required
✅ Strong work ethic and reliability
✅ Early Morning Starts
✅ Physically fit and able to pass a Drug & Alcohol test and Police Check
✅ Ready to start immediately

Key Responsibilities
  • Visiting local supermarkets to merchandise bakery products
  • Following planograms to stock shelves
  • Checking and rotating stock, removing expired or damaged items
  • Maintaining a clean and tidy product display
  • Completing basic paperwork as required
  • Ensuring products such as bread, muffins, and crumpets are well presented and available for customers
What’s on Offer
✨ Ongoing flexible casual work with a trusted national brand
✨ Great hourly rate
✨ Opportunity to work close to home
✨ Comprehensive face-to-face training provided
✨ Pathway to a permanent role for the right candidate

job.title: Senior Cyber Security Engineer - Network - Akamai
job.description:
Are you an experienced Cyber Security Engineer with strong expertise in network and edge security platforms? We are seeking a highly skilled professional to join our client AGL supporting critical customer-facing digital services and security infrastructure. This is a six months contract opportunity in Melbourne CBD in a hybrid working environment.

This is an exciting contract opportunity for a cyber security specialist who has hands-on experience with Akamai and enterprise security technologies and enjoys working across complex environments to enhance security posture, resilience, and operational excellence.

Key Responsibilities
  • Administer, maintain and optimise enterprise web application and edge security platforms.
  • Implement security platform changes in alignment with enterprise change management, peer review and release governance processes.
  • Develop and support automation initiatives using APIs, Terraform and other approved tools to improve operational efficiency and reduce configuration risks.
  • Monitor, investigate and respond to security incidents escalated from service desk and security operations teams.
  • Assess, communicate, mitigate and track platform-related security risks and incidents.
  • Collaborate closely with cyber security, infrastructure, network, architecture and operational teams to deliver secure and resilient services.
  • Support critical customer-facing platforms operating in a 24x7 environment.
  • Participate in major incident management and on-call support activities as required.
  • Provide technical guidance and recommendations to ensure security platforms meet regulatory, compliance and industry security requirements.
  • Contribute to continuous improvement initiatives across security engineering, operations and platform management.
Skills & Experience Essential

  • Strong hands-on experience with Akamai security solutions, including:
    • Web Application Firewall (WAF)
    • Edge DNS
    • Bot Management
    • API Security
    • Traffic Management
    • DDoS Protection
  • Akamai Certified Security Administrator or equivalent certification, with proven experience administering enterprise security and WAF platforms.
  • Experience with alternative edge security technologies such as Cloudflare, Imperva, or similar enterprise platforms.
  • Demonstrated experience within cyber security engineering, security operations, or platform administration roles in large and complex environments.
  • Strong understanding of:
    • Network Security
    • Identity & Access Management (IAM)
    • Endpoint Security
    • Threat Detection & Monitoring
    • Encryption Technologies
    • Vulnerability Management
    • Security Operations Practices
  • Excellent stakeholder engagement and communication skills with the ability to influence and collaborate across technical and business teams.
  • Experience supporting mission-critical, highly available digital services.
Desirable
  • Experience working in regulated or critical infrastructure environments.
  • Knowledge of security frameworks and standards including:
    • Essential Eight
    • NIST Cyber Security Framework
    • SOCI obligations
    • Australian security and risk management practices
  • Experience with Infrastructure as Code (Terraform) and security automation.
